_comment: AI players (Homestead's own). The AI knows the whole map. Every thinkSeconds it starts at most one building: the first entry of buildOrder whose count it has not reached and which it can place (enough free planks and stones, a fitting spot on own land). Entries that need a resource (trees, stones, ore, water, fish) are skipped while the own land lacks it - the expansion then builds towers towards it.
_housingComment: A living house is started when fewer carriers than freeCarriers are available (residents still to come count as available).
_stockComment: A storehouse is built once a smith or gold melt works and stockWhenWaiting units of goods worth storing (storage.materials in production.json: tools, weapons, gold) lie around and the storehouses have fewer than two free piles.
_expansionComment: Towers towards what the own land lacks, in this order: quarry stone below minStoneUnits, none of the listed ores, stone below wantedStoneUnits, trees below minTrees, no water; towards free land when a building found no room; with spareSoldiersForLand idle soldiers and landStock planks and stones beyond the tower's cost simply towards the nearest free land. The tower goes to the own-land spot nearest the target. While a needed tower cannot be afforded, the economy keeps its planks and stones back.
